speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are presenting with a chest skin lesion. To better understand your condition, how long have you had this lesion, and has its appearance or size changed recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age, the 2-month duration, and the reported increase in size of this painless chest lesion, is the lesion changing color or developing an ulcerated center? Also, do you have a personal or family history of melanoma or other skin cancers?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin lesion on the chest. I also have Lesion has increased in size, Not painful, Not itchy.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lesion has remained painless and without itching; has it changed in color, developed a scaly border, or begun to bleed or ulcerate? Additionally, have you noticed any recent changes in your sun exposure or use of tanning beds?

REQUEST TEST: Dermoscopy of chest lesion.
REQUEST IMAGES: Clinical_photo_chest_lesion

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dermoscopy of chest lesion: Irregularly pigmented lesion with asymmetric distribution of brown and black colors. Presence of an atypical pigment network, irregular dots/globules, and a blue-white veil noted at the periphery. Vascular structures appear irregular. No clear evidence of ulceration or bleeding on surface visualization. Clinical_photo_chest_lesion: Single lesion on the anterior chest wall. Lesion is asymmetrical with irregular, notched borders. Color variegation present including light brown, dark brown, and black. Diameter is estimated at approximately 7mm. Surface appears slightly elevated and firm; no visible scaling or ulceration. Patient denies recent sun exposure or tanning bed use.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, glaucoma Social history: Smokes 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the last 40 years, drinks two to three beers on weekends

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent weight loss, fever, fatigue, or changes in appetite. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lesion has not changed color, scaly border, bled, or ulcerated, and you deny systemic symptoms like weight loss or fever; given your age, diabetes, and the recent growth of a painless chest lesion, have you noticed any new lumps or swelling in your neck, armpits, or above your collarbone?

REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_Abdomen_Pelvis
REQUEST IMAGES: Histopathology_slides

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_Chest_Abdomen_Pelvis: No evidence of regional lymphadenopathy, distant metastasis, or other suspicious masses in the thoracic, abdominal, or pelvic cavities. Histopathology_slides: Biopsy of the chest lesion confirms malignant melanoma, characterized by atypical melanocytes infiltrating the epidermis and dermis, with significant asymmetry, irregular borders, and color variegation.
